# Maximus Design System Platform

**Version:** 0.23.0 | **Status:** Pre-release · Phase 3 — Components

`@mms/design-system` is a governed, themeable, WCAG 2.1 AA component library built as Lit web
components. It works in plain HTML, any bundler, and React.

## Quickstart

Requires Maximus VPN. No credentials, no auth token, no JFrog account.

```
npm config set "@mms:registry=https://artifactory.mars.pcf-maximus.com/artifactory/api/npm/mms-ds-platform/" --location=project
npm install @mms/design-system
```

> Keep the double quotes — Windows PowerShell drops the argument without them.
> Copy the command exactly: nothing in it is a placeholder, and `--location=project` is a
> literal npm flag meaning "write `.npmrc` into this folder."

**Just want to see it run?** One more command — it writes an `index.html`, serves it, and opens
your browser. No bundler, no config, no files to create by hand:

```
npx mms-ds start
```

The page starts on the Maximus brand. Add `--theme va-gov` to start on another one — every
theme ships inside the bundle, so switching costs nothing.

**Adding it to a page you already have?** One script tag gives you every component, all icons,
all tokens, and Lit itself — nothing else to install:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="maximus">
  <body>
    <mms-button variant="primary" label="Save"></mms-button>
    <script type="module" src="./node_modules/@mms/design-system/dist/standalone.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

Serve it over HTTP — browsers refuse module scripts on `file://`.

**Using a bundler?** Import per component — this is the production path and tree-shakes:

```js
import '@mms/design-system/tokens.css';
import '@mms/design-system/themes/maximus';
import '@mms/design-system/components/mms-button';
```

Then set `data-theme` on `<html>` (see [Theming](#theming)) and use `<mms-button>` anywhere.

---

## Dependencies

| | What |
|---|---|
| **You install** | Node.js 20+ and npm 10+. That is the entire list. |
| **npm installs for you** | `lit` — a peer dependency, auto-installed by npm 7+. Do not run `npm install lit`. |
| **Only for React** | `react`, `react-dom`, `@lit/react` — optional peers, add them yourself. |
| **You never need** | JFrog credentials, an auth token, or a `~/.npmrc` entry. Read access is anonymous. If something asks you for credentials, it is a symptom of a different problem. |

The package has **zero runtime dependencies**.

---

## Entry points

| Import | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `@mms/design-system/components/mms-<name>` | Production. Tree-shakes to only what you use. |
| `@mms/design-system/standalone` | Prototyping with no build step. Self-contained, includes Lit. |
| `@mms/design-system` | Convenience barrel — registers all 28 elements. Needs a bundler. |
| `@mms/design-system/react` | React binding. Requires `@lit/react`. |
| `@mms/design-system/tokens.css` | Structural tokens. Required for the bundler path. |
| `@mms/design-system/themes/<theme>` | Brand tokens. Required for the bundler path. |

One command, not an import:

| Command | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `npx mms-ds start` | Scaffold `index.html`, serve it, open the browser. Prototyping, zero config. |
| `npx mms-ds init` | Scaffold `index.html` only — bring your own server. |
| `npx mms-ds start --theme va-gov` | Start on a different brand. `npx mms-ds --help` lists what's installed. |

## Components

28 custom elements, all prefixed `mms-`:

```
mms-accordion        mms-accordion-item   mms-alert-banner     mms-breadcrumbs
mms-button           mms-card             mms-checkbox         mms-checkbox-group
mms-drawer           mms-icon             mms-inline-alert     mms-link
mms-modal            mms-multi-select     mms-progress-bar     mms-radio
mms-radio-group      mms-select           mms-status-tag       mms-stepper
mms-tabs             mms-tabs-item        mms-tag              mms-text-area
mms-text-field       mms-toast            mms-toggle           mms-tooltip
```

### Machine-readable API

Every component's props, attributes, slots, events, and CSS custom properties are described in
**`custom-elements.json`** at the package root — the [Custom Elements Manifest](https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest)
standard, referenced by the `customElements` field in `package.json`.

**If you are an AI assistant generating code against this library, read that file.** It is the
authoritative spec and ships with every version, so it can never drift from the code you have
installed.

```
node_modules/@mms/design-system/custom-elements.json
```

---

## Theming

Themes are activated by attributes on the root element — not by a JavaScript API.

```html
<html data-theme="maximus">
```

| Attribute | Values | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `data-theme` | `default`, `maximus`, `va-gov`, `uss-oh-dvs` | Yes — without it brand tokens do not resolve and components render unstyled |
| `data-mode` | `light`, `dark` | No — omit it to follow the browser, see below |
| `data-density` | `default`, `compact` | No |

Put `data-theme` and `data-mode` on the **same element**. Splitting them across `<html>` and
`<body>` is not supported.

### Dark mode

**If you omit `data-mode`, the theme follows the user's OS/browser setting** via
`prefers-color-scheme`. No JavaScript required — it is a media query in the theme CSS.
Setting `data-mode` opts out of that and pins the mode:

```html
<html data-theme="maximus">                    <!-- follows the browser -->
<html data-theme="maximus" data-mode="light">  <!-- always light -->
<html data-theme="maximus" data-mode="dark">   <!-- always dark -->
```

Auto-following requires the dark sheet to be loaded. On the bundler path import both
`@mms/design-system/themes/maximus` and `@mms/design-system/themes/maximus-dark` — with only
the light sheet there is nothing for the media query to apply. The standalone build includes
every theme, so it works with no imports at all and defaults to `data-theme="maximus"` if you
set nothing.

---

## Architecture

### Token model

Strict two-layer separation:

- **Layer 1 — Structural tokens** — Maximus-owned, fixed across all engagements. Spacing, neutral colors, utility colors, radius, elevation, motion, breakpoints, focus-ring, type scale structure.
- **Layer 2 — Brand token sheets** — Client-owned, standalone per engagement. Each brand sheet is a complete definition conforming to the structural contract — not an override layer.

### Accessibility

All components target WCAG 2.1 AA. Compliance is enforced structurally via token contracts, not
manual review. Section 508 applies to federal engagements; ADA Title II applies to state
engagements.

### Technology

Lit · TypeScript · Storybook 10 · Style Dictionary · CSS Custom Properties. Prior art: Marina
(Chubb Design System — Forrester-recognized).

### Distribution roadmap

`@mms/design-system` is the one published package and serves every web platform today. Purpose-built
packages for platforms that cannot consume npm — `@mms/aem-clientlib`, `@mms/drupal-module`,
`@mms/salesforce`, `@mms/tokens-ios`, `@mms/tokens-android` — are Phase 4 scope and **are not yet
published**. Do not attempt to install them.

## Version History

### v0.23.0 (Current — Pre-release) — 2026-08-21

**React Distribution**
- Every component now ships a typed React binding. Coverage goes from 2 hand-written wrappers to all 28, generated by `scripts/generate-react.mjs` from `custom-elements.json` and wired into `npm run build`, so a new component cannot ship without a binding (DS-168)
- Every custom event detail payload across 18 components is now an exported type dispatched via `new CustomEvent<T>`. The shapes existed only as JSDoc prose before, so no consumer could type against them — this benefits plain TypeScript custom-element users identically, React only made the gap visible (DS-168)
- New `/react-wrappers` skill — 4 gates covering applicability, drift, typecheck and a render smoke test. It runs the generator and reviews the output; it never authors a binding by hand (DS-168)

**Components**
- Fixed `input`, `focus` and `blur` firing **twice** per interaction on `mms-text-field`, `mms-text-area`, `mms-select` and `mms-multi-select`. The inner control's native events are `composed`, so they crossed the shadow boundary and landed on the same host listener as the component's own `CustomEvent`. The duplicate carries no payload, so a consumer reading `detail.value` got `undefined` and silently overwrote good state. `mms-select` additionally leaked a native `input` alongside `change` (DS-168)
- Fixed the same symptom from a different mechanism on `mms-radio-group` — a slotted `mms-radio`'s own bubbling `change` surfaced on the group under the group's declared event name (DS-168)
- New event-boundary regression tests count deliveries and name the constructor sequence, so the two mechanisms stay distinguishable. Every other test in those files passed with or without the guard, which is why this hid (DS-168)

**Platform Tooling**
- This repo had **never type-checked**. There was no `typecheck` script and no `tsc` in CI; esbuild powers the build, Vitest and Storybook, and all three strip types without checking them. `npx tsc --noEmit` reported 9 pre-existing errors. Added `typecheck` and `typecheck:react` scripts, wired both into CI, and modelled the new gate in `verify-gates.mjs` so it is proven live rather than assumed (DS-170)
- Fixed the 9 errors. One was a real disabled guardrail: `Stepper.stories.ts` `.slice()`d its substeps literal before assignment, widening `state` from the `StepperItemState` union to plain `string` — an invalid state would have raised no error and rendered a silently unstyled substep (DS-170)
- Version single-sourcing — the version string was hardcoded in six files, two of which are not on the main-branch allowlist, so `/update-docs` could not complete its own job on `main` without a feature branch. Both Installation pages now derive it from `package.json` at render time (DS-170)
- New `scripts/check-lockfile-scope.mjs`, run from both `.husky/pre-commit` and `protect-branches.sh` — `package-lock.json` is allowlisted on `main` for the version bump only, and this rejects any lockfile change there that touches anything but the two root `version` fields. A dependency add, remove or upgrade still requires a feature branch and a PR (DS-170)

### v0.22.0 (Pre-release) — 2026-08-21

**⚠️ Breaking**
- `@lit/react` moved from `dependencies` to an optional `peerDependency`. React consumers must add it explicitly: `npm install @mms/design-system @lit/react react react-dom`. Non-React consumers stop paying a 1.9MB tax (`@lit/react` + `@types/react` + `csstype`) for code they never execute — `dependencies` is now empty, and `lit` is the only required peer, auto-installed by npm 7+ (DS-163)

**Packaging & Distribution**
- Fixed the barrel import bundling to **zero bytes** — `sideEffects` omitted `index.js`, so bundlers treated the barrel as side-effect-free and dropped the module before reaching the component files where the marking would have applied (DS-163)
- New `./standalone` entry point — a self-contained esbuild bundle with Lit, every component, tokens and all 8 theme/mode sheets inlined. Runs from a plain `<script type="module">` with no build step (DS-163)
- New `mms-ds` CLI — `npx mms-ds start` scaffolds a themed page and serves it; no project, no install, no files to create (DS-163)
- `uss-oh-dvs` theme exports added — the CSS already shipped in the tarball, but the exports map never listed it, so exports gating blocked the import (DS-163)
- Auto dark mode — `dist` theme sheets now emit a `prefers-color-scheme` copy keyed on `:not([data-mode])`, so every no-JS distribution path honours the OS setting. An explicit `data-mode` still wins, with no JS and no flash (DS-163)
- `engines` field added (node >=20, npm >=10) (DS-163)

**Components**
- New `mms-multi-select` component (DS-157)
- New `mms-drawer` component, plus the stepper's radial "view all steps" drawer interaction (DS-161)
- New `mms-progress-bar` component — determinate (DS-054)
- `warning` accepted as an alias for `caution` across `mms-alert-banner`, `mms-inline-alert`, `mms-status-tag` and `mms-toast`. It previously fell through to informational styling, so the severity announced to a screen reader stopped matching the severity intended (DS-163)
- `mms-tabs-item`'s fill-active label moved from the fixed-white `--color-text-on-emphasis` to the per-theme `--color-text-on-primary` — it measured 4.17:1 against a 4.5:1 floor in dark mode, in all four themes (DS-163)

**Accessibility**
- a11y coverage axes now multiply rather than sitting in a flat list. Colour mode, variant and density multiply against states; the flat model counted 6 cells where there were 8 and reported full coverage. The grid grew by 162 rows, all passing (DS-163)
- `validate-color-scheme` upgraded from `console.warn` to `console.error` — warn is filtered from most consumer consoles by default and never fails a test run, so an invalid theme × colorScheme combination rendered silently (DS-163)

**Platform Tooling**
- `scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` retired, its sweep merged into `contrast-check.mjs`. The old script read a colour table hardcoded inside itself, reporting 296 green checks while reading no files at all — no theme regression of any kind could reach it. The replacement resolves real `var()` chains out of `src/themes/*.css` across all 4 themes × light/dark, with an adjacency model so a border is measured against the surface a control sits on: 58 pairs + 1408 sweep checks, 0 failures (DS-163)
- New `scripts/verify-gates.mjs` — applies one surgical mutation per CI gate and asserts the gate goes red. 8 LIVE, 0 DISCONNECTED. Runs in CI (DS-163)
- Fixed `validate:tokens` and `audit:hardcoded` throwing on Node 20 before running a single check — both used a glob API unavailable there (DS-163)
- Two token bindings corrected by role: `--color-action-text` (step 9 Solid → step 12 Text) and `--color-action-text-hover` (step 10 → step 11 Text muted). Steps 9/10 are fills you place text *on*, not text colours (DS-163)

**Documentation**
- Developer Guide → Installation rewritten cross-platform. Every command is copy-pasteable on macOS zsh, PowerShell, cmd.exe and Git Bash — the old guide's bash-only `\` line continuation silently stripped `--registry` on Windows and produced a permissions-flavoured 404 that looked like an auth problem and was not one (DS-163)
- New Themes page documenting the typography contract — a theme names its typeface, it does not carry the file (DS-163)
- README restructured AI-first: quickstart in the first 20 lines, every component tag name, the `data-theme` / `data-mode` contract, and an explicit pointer to `custom-elements.json` as the authoritative machine-readable spec (DS-163)
